atoms.text: This procedure configures the IAM role NetTraceDeliveryRole so that the NetTrace flow-record service can write log files into the bucket example-netflow-logs. The role's trust policy names the NetTrace service principal, which lets the service assume the role at the start of each delivery. Access is granted entirely by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Create a customer-managed policy with a statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-netflow-logs/flows/* and attach it to NetTraceDeliveryRole. Add a second statement that allows s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::example-netflow-logs, so the service can resolve the bucket's Region before it writes. Do not edit the bucket policy for this setup, because the permissions on the role are sufficient for same-account delivery. NetTrace writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under flows/YYYY/MM/DD/, and it writes to no other prefix. To verify, trigger a test delivery from the NetTrace console and confirm that an object appears under flows/ with the expected timestamp. If the delivery reports AccessDenied, check that the resource ARN ends in /* and that the policy is attached to the role.

This procedure configures the bucket example-netflow-logs so that the NetTrace flow-record service can write log files into it using the IAM role NetTraceDeliveryRole. The role's trust policy names the NetTrace service principal, which lets the service assume the role at the start of each delivery. Access is granted entirely by the bucket's resource-based policy, and no S3 permissions are attached to the role itself. Add a bucket policy statement with Effect set to Allow, Principal set to the ARN of NetTraceDeliveryRole, and Action set to s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-netflow-logs/flows/*. Add a second statement for the same principal that allows s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::example-netflow-logs, so the service can resolve the bucket's Region before it writes. Do not attach an S3 policy to the role, because the bucket policy statement names the role directly and is sufficient for same-account delivery. NetTrace writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under flows/YYYY/MM/DD/, and it writes to no other prefix. To verify, trigger a test delivery from the NetTrace console and confirm that an object appears under flows/ with the expected timestamp. If the delivery reports AccessDenied, check that the resource ARN ends in /* and that the Principal ARN matches the role exactly.

This guide covers an on-premises log shipper called LogRelay that uploads application logs to the bucket example-app-logs using the IAM user logrelay-agent. The agent runs on a host outside the cloud network and authenticates with an access key pair that belongs to this user. Access is granted solely by an identity-based policy attached to logrelay-agent, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a policy with one statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-app-logs/app/* and attach it directly to the user. The statement does not include s3:GetObject or s3:DeleteObject, so the agent can add files but cannot read or remove them. Store the access key in the LogRelay configuration file with permissions restricted to the service account that runs the agent. LogRelay uploads a rotated log file each time a file reaches 50 MB, using keys of the form app/hostname/filename.log.gz. After the first upload, list the app/ prefix from an administrator session and confirm that the object size matches the local file.

This procedure sets up an append-only audit trail in the bucket example-audit-trail, which the AuditStream service fills with event records from two Regions. The service assumes the IAM role AuditStreamWriter, and that role is the only principal that delivers to the bucket. Access is granted by an identity-based policy attached to AuditStreamWriter, and the bucket policy remains as it was. The policy contains one statement that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/audit/us-east/* and arn:aws:s3:::example-audit-trail/audit/eu-west/*. It deliberately omits s3:DeleteObject and s3:PutObjectVersionTagging, so delivered records cannot be removed or relabeled through this role. AuditStream writes a JSON file every ten minutes per Region, and each key ends with the file's sequence number. Enable bucket versioning before the first delivery so that an accidental overwrite keeps the earlier version. To test, request a manual flush in the AuditStream console and confirm that one new object appears in each Region prefix.

This guide explains how to let the EdgeBalancer access-log feature deliver request logs to the bucket example-lb-logs. EdgeBalancer assumes the IAM role EdgeLogDelivery when it publishes a log batch. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to EdgeLogDelivery, and no change is made to the bucket policy. The policy allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-lb-logs/edge/111122223333/*, where the path segment is the account ID that owns the load balancers. When logging is enabled, EdgeBalancer first writes a small object named delivery-check.txt at that prefix to confirm that it has write access. If this check fails, the console refuses to enable logging and displays the S3 error code. After the check passes, the service delivers a compressed log file for each load balancer every five minutes. Confirm the setup by sending a few requests through a load balancer and looking for a new file under the edge/ prefix after about ten minutes.

This procedure gives two IAM roles access to the bucket example-platform-logs: PlatformLogWriter, which the delivery service uses to write logs, and LogIndexerRole, which a search indexer uses to read them. Both grants are made through identity-based policies attached to the respective roles, and the bucket policy is not changed. Attach a policy to PlatformLogWriter that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-platform-logs/delivered/*. Attach a separate policy to LogIndexerRole that allows s3:GetObject on the same prefix and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-platform-logs with an s3:prefix condition of delivered/*. The indexer therefore reads exactly the files the writer produces and cannot read other prefixes. The writer places a new file every minute, and the indexer polls the prefix listing every two minutes and downloads files it has not yet processed. To validate, deliver a test file and confirm that the indexer log records its key within one polling interval. If the indexer lists but cannot download, verify that the GetObject resource uses the object ARN rather than the bucket ARN.

This guide configures the container platform PodShip to deliver large log archives to the bucket example-pod-logs using the IAM role PodShipDelivery. PodShip splits archives above 100 MB into parts and uploads them as multipart uploads. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to PodShipDelivery, and the bucket policy is left as it is. The policy needs s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-pod-logs/pods/*, so a failed upload can be cleaned up by the same role. It also needs s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::example-pod-logs, which PodShip calls before it resumes an interrupted upload. Without the abort permission, incomplete parts remain in the bucket and incur storage charges until a lifecycle rule removes them. Add a lifecycle rule that aborts incomplete multipart uploads after seven days as a safeguard. Test by delivering an archive larger than 100 MB and confirm that a single complete object appears under pods/ with no pending multipart uploads.

This procedure lets the IAM role SecLogDelivery write security logs to the bucket example-sec-logs under a rule that every object must be encrypted on arrival. The delivery service sends the header x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256 with each upload. Access is granted exclusively by an identity-based policy attached to SecLogDelivery, and the bucket policy is not altered. The policy statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-sec-logs/security/* and includes a StringEquals condition on s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption with the value AES256. A request that omits the header or specifies another value does not match the statement and is denied. Set the bucket's default encryption to AES256 as well, so objects written by other means are also encrypted. The service writes one file per hour under security/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/. To test, deliver a sample batch and confirm in the object properties that encryption is reported as AES256. If every upload fails, check in the delivery settings that the encryption option is enabled.

This guide gives a support engineer read-only access to delivered DNS query logs in the bucket example-dns-logs, which the ResolverLens service populates. The engineer signs in as the IAM user support-reader to download files while diagnosing resolution failures. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to support-reader, and the bucket policy is not changed. The policy allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-logs with an s3:prefix condition of resolver/*, and s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-dns-logs/resolver/*. It grants no write or delete actions, so the user cannot alter or remove delivered files. ResolverLens writes one file per resolver endpoint every fifteen minutes, with keys such as resolver/endpoint-id/YYYY/MM/DD/HHMM.log.gz. To check the setup, sign in as support-reader, list resolver/ for the current day, and download the newest file. A request for any key outside resolver/ should return AccessDenied, which confirms the prefix restriction works.
